devices.name: Logix Artemis 32 KiB professional video card

specification.mode_discovery: Enumerate controller modes intersected with identified or configured monitor raster capabilities and available buffering/sprite allocations. Reject unsupported downscaling.

memory_layout.mode_exclusivity: Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of 32 KiB display DRAM. Exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM is available in every mode.
memory_layout.font_policy: One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.
memory_layout.page_flip: Latch selected page during vertical blank; drawing throughput is not guaranteed by double buffering.

sprites.coordinate_space: Logical mode pixels; scale together with the background. Signed 16-bit X and Y; clip at screen edges.
sprites.priority: Lower sprite number wins; all sprites overlay background/text.
sprites.registers: Two descriptor banks hold signed 16-bit X/Y, enable and reserved controls. CPU/DMA uses auto-incrementing SRAM upload ports.
sprites.updates: Switch descriptor bank atomically at vertical blank. Pattern writes require scheduled access or disabling affected sprites; 1 KiB does not hold two complete pattern sets.
sprites.allocation_policy: Five sprites in every text/bitmap mode, including double-buffered backgrounds. Sprite SRAM never consumes display DRAM.
sprites.descriptor_allocation_note: 80 bytes of live two-bank descriptors within a 128-byte reserved area; 48 bytes padding. 640 pattern + 128 descriptor + 256 scratch bytes = 1024.

display_memory.organization: 16K × 16 bits; ordinary external DRAM, independent display refresh sequencer.

pixel_buffer.location: On video ASIC; SRAM banks with page ownership latches
pixel_buffer.policy: Eight-pixel parallel renderer fills free pages; independent clocked serializer drains ready pages. Two pages per 640-pixel line; prefill before active display; never overwrite displaying pages. Underflow blanks pixels, preserves sync and sets sticky fault.
pixel_buffer.physical_organization: Each 160-byte bank is 40 words × 32 bits. Load eight 4-bit pixels into a separate 32-bit serializer latch every eight dot clocks, then shift at 21.504 MHz. SRAM array reads run at 2.688 MHz, not one read per dot; filler and drain use different banks.

character_row_cache.purpose: Current and next 80-column character/attribute row; separate from 640-byte pixel FIFO.

timing_budget.qualification: At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

specification.arbitration: Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.
specification.monitor_policy: Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

manufacturing_requirements: Dedicated slot; powered-off replacement only; host interface, power rails and signal integrity require qualification.

dated_revisions.name: COMDEX 1982 professional graphics revision
dated_revisions.status: Accepted offering specification; production and driver acceptance required before shipment. June specifications and cost snapshot remain the earlier baseline.
dated_revisions.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
dated_revisions.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
dated_revisions.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
dated_revisions.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
dated_revisions.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.
dated_revisions.cost_boundary: November revision assessed separately in comdex_1982_cost_review.json. June cost rows unchanged; quotes and production qualification pending.

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Qualify revised deflection, analog grayscale amplifier and high-speed digital link; no stock-monitor plug compatibility or final OEM contract assumed.
specification.availability: Around June 1982; supersedes the proposed January prototype delivery.

dated_revisions.name: Logix Mono Pro 17 — HD17H analog OEM configuration
dated_revisions.oem: Ball HD-series HD17H, 17-inch horizontal-format OEM assembly, analog/linear-video option
dated_revisions.signal_path: Logix digital pixel index -> AION palette/controller -> 4-bit intensity DAC -> level-matched Ball analog input and linear amplifier. TTL/ECL-only input is not sufficient.
dated_revisions.rgb_palette_mapping: Preserve the 12-bit RGB command format. For grayscale, equal-channel values 000,111,...,FFF map to the corresponding 16 intensity codes. Other RGB values use a documented fixed luminance mapping, with DAC/gamma calibration qualified on the actual CRT.
